prompt.content:
You are writing internal knowledge-base articles for an enterprise support team, for a synthetic dataset used to build and evaluate KB-recommendation systems. For each article brief in the input JSON array, write a TITLE, a one-to-two sentence CONTENT_SUMMARY (what an agent sees in search results), and a CONTENT_BODY of 3-6 short sentences (a practical troubleshooting note: what to check, what usually causes it, how it's typically resolved) consistent with the given category/symptoms/root causes/resolutions. Vary style: some articles are broad and reference-like, some are narrowly specific with numbered steps. If "outdated" is true, the body should read like guidance that predates a later product change (e.g. reference an older flow) without literally saying "this article is outdated".

Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"articles": [{"i": <int>, "title": "...", "content_summary": "...", "content_body": "..."}, ...]} covering every article index, in any order.

[{'i': 0, 'category': 'Data / Corruption', 'subcategory_names': ['data out of sync', 'corrupted export file', 'data truncation'], 'symptom_names': ['data mismatch', 'user reports data loss', 'corrupted export', 'duplicate records', 'missing records', 'missing data'], 'root_cause_names': ['data quality issue', 'product defect', 'idempotency/duplicate-processing failure'], 'resolution_names': ['product patch', 'engineering escalation', 'known-issue workaround', 'data repair script', 'queue reprocessing', 'manual reconciliation'], 'product_names': ['Notification Hub', 'Fee Analyzer'], 'specificity': 'broad', 'outdated': False}]

response: {"articles": [{"i": 0, "title": "Troubleshooting Data Mismatches and Corruption in Notification Hub and Fee Analyzer", "content_summary": "Guidance for identifying and resolving data synchronization issues, corrupted exports, and record discrepancies across Notification Hub and Fee Analyzer.", "content_body": "Data mismatches or missing records often stem from idempotency failures or quality issues during processing. First, check for duplicate records or truncation signs in export files. If standard reconciliation fails, run the data repair script or reprocess the affected queue. For persistent issues confirmed as product defects, escalate to engineering for a patch or known-issue workaround."}]}
